title: Yash Breaks Down Ramayana’s Rs 4,000 Crore Budget: Both Films Plus Hollywood-Style Promotions
excerpt: The actor and co-producer explains that India’s most expensive film project includes global release costs across both parts, as the team mounts CinemaCon and Comic-Con campaigns to position the epic for worldwide audiences.
body:
• Yash, who plays Ravana and co-produces the film, clarified on Aap Ki Adalat that the widely reported Rs 4,000 crore figure covers both parts of Ramayana plus global release and promotional costs, not the production budget of Part 1 alone.
  • The film's promotional campaign has already included appearances at CinemaCon in Las Vegas and San Diego Comic-Con, with posters displayed alongside Hollywood's biggest upcoming releases.
  • Ramayana Part 1, starring Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama and Sai Pallavi as Sita, is set for a worldwide theatrical release on November 6, 2026, timed with Diwali.
  • Producer Namit Malhotra has rejected a record Rs 700 crore OTT bid, reportedly holding out for Rs 1,000 crore as confidence builds around the film's global box office potential.

Superstar Yash has finally put numbers in context for Ramayana's eye-popping budget, explaining that the Rs 4,000 crore figure circulating in trade circles covers far more than cameras and sets.

Speaking on Rajat Sharma's Aap Ki Adalat, Yash — who plays the demon king Ravana and serves as co-producer alongside Namit Malhotra — said the amount encompasses both parts of director Nitesh Tiwari's epic adaptation plus their global release and promotional expenses. He described the accounting approach as "Hollywood math," where significant spending on marketing and worldwide distribution is baked into the headline budget because the films are designed for a global audience.

The Biggest Indian Film Ever Made

Even with Yash's clarification, the numbers are staggering. At approximately $500 million across both parts, Ramayana stands as the most expensive Indian film project in history, dwarfing previous benchmarks. No released Indian film has crossed Rs 1,000 crore in production budget, making this a venture without precedent in the country's cinema industry.

Producer Namit Malhotra, CEO of Prime Focus, has been emphatic about the film's ambitions. "We're making the largest film in the world for the greatest story, the greatest epic, that the world should see," he said in an earlier interview. "It's meant for the world and it's got the best of the East and the best of the West coming together to make it happen."

"If the expenditure is global, the revenue opportunity is also global. Ramayana and Toxic are attempts to position Indian cinema as a truly global cinematic force."

— Yash, on Aap Ki Adalat

Hollywood-Scale Promotion

The global ambition is not just talk. Ramayana's promotional campaign has already taken the film to two of Hollywood's biggest industry events. Yash and Malhotra presented the project at CinemaCon 2026 in Las Vegas in April, where Ramayana posters were displayed alongside promotions for upcoming titles from Marvel, DC and other major studios.

In July, Ranbir Kapoor and Yash appeared together at San Diego Comic-Con, marking a first for an Indian film at the convention. "I've always been a fan of comic conventions," Kapoor told Reuters. "To finally be here on the other side with a story which is so ingrained in our culture, to bring that to a larger audience, it's really a proud moment for our entire team."

Yash called Comic-Con "the right kind of crowd who really understand the nuances of this kind of film and the effort that goes behind it."

Record OTT Bid Rejected

The financial confidence extends to distribution deals. According to Bollywood Hungama, Malhotra rejected a record Rs 700 crore OTT bid for both films — the highest ever for an Indian production — and is reportedly holding out for Rs 1,000 crore. The remaining Rs 3,000 crore would need to be recovered from theatrical revenue and other sources.

The strategy mirrors how Hollywood studios manage tent-pole franchises: hold back on early deals, build anticipation through event marketing and let the escalating buzz drive up prices.

A Diaspora Event Film

For the Indian diaspora, Ramayana is shaping up as a cultural event as much as a movie release. The film adapts the Valmiki Ramayana, one of Hinduism's most revered epics, with a cast designed to bridge Indian and international audiences: Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Sunny Deol as Hanuman and Ravi Dubey as Lakshmana.

"It will promise a very different experience unlike anything traditionally that Indian movies offer or even Hollywood for that matter."

— Namit Malhotra, Producer

Part 1 will release simultaneously in India and the United States on November 6, timed with Diwali. The film will be available in multiple languages, with the makers reportedly using AI-powered lip-syncing technology for English, Spanish and Japanese versions. Part 2 is expected during Diwali 2027.

What to Watch

With Yash's action thriller Toxic arriving on August 26, Sunny Deol's Batwara 1947 already in theaters and Sai Pallavi's OM releasing in October, the Ramayana ensemble will dominate Indian cinema's most competitive quarter. The film's ability to cross over to non-Indian audiences — the central bet behind the Rs 4,000 crore investment — will be the story to follow.
